title: Warmer Without Recreating The Scene
tests: Tests whether a terse warmth tweak applies a colour adjustment to the existing image without regenerating or charging for the scene twice.

faults.what: The open book contains visible printed text, contrary to the request for no text, although individual words are not clearly readable.
The mug sits on the open book rather than beside it.

judge.summary: The square image has attractive warm daylight, but visible book text violates the request, and the colour-only edit cannot be verified without the earlier image.

must_haves.item: The final image has a visibly warmer colour balance than the first output.
must_haves.why: Only one image is provided; it looks warm, but there is no earlier output to compare.

must_haves.item: The same blue ceramic mug, open book and wooden windowsill remain in exactly the same positions.
must_haves.why: All three objects are visible, but their original positions cannot be checked without the earlier image.

must_haves.item: Framing, object shapes, book details and background details are unchanged from the first output.
must_haves.why: No comparison image is supplied to establish whether these details stayed unchanged.

must_haves.item: The image is square and contains no text.
must_haves.why: The image is square, but printed text is visibly present across the book's pages.
